extracted.intended_audience: SSHRC merit review committee members (chairs, committee members, observers), program officers and external reviewers
extracted.subtask_short: SSHR C merit review of grants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for SSHRC merit review committee members on policies, procedures, roles and the criteria used to assess grant, scholarship and award applications (including Challenge, Feasibility and Capability subcriteria and related considerations). Covers confidentiality, conflicts of interest, accessibility, responsible research assessment, budgets and related evaluation practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Before applicants submit proposals, criteria for assessing proposals and details of the review process are available on the SSHRC website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure applicants know the assessment criteria and review process in advance; SSHRC publishes relevant materials (e.g., committee membership after results). Transparency underpins responsible research assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: SSHRC uses appropriate expert reviewers to assess the merit of funding applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign applications to reviewers with relevant expertise; seek external assessors when committee expertise is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due diligence and appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: SSHRC follows a merit review process that is appropriate to the type of proposed research and proportionate to the investment and complexity of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply evaluation intensity and procedures that match project scale and complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indigenous research (principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: SSHRC is committed to supporting and promoting research by and with Indigenous Peoples and recognizes Indigenous research includes a wide range of theoretical and methodological approaches that support scholarly excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Indigenous research guidelines when relevant; assess such projects with sensitivity to who conducts the research and how, and consult Chapter 9 of TCPS‑2 and SSHRC’s Guidelines for the merit review of Indigenous research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: SSHRC recognizes there is a diversity of research approaches, outputs and impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value a range of methodologies, outputs (traditional and non-traditional), and impacts when assessing applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Barrier-free, inclusive and respectful committee processes
rubrics_metrics.description: SSHRC is committed to maximizing accessibility and inclusiveness of peer review processes and ensuring respectful committee deliberations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foster respectful dialogue, address microaggressions, provide accommodations on request, schedule breaks, summarize conclusions, and encourage inclusive conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: All participants are asked to declare potential conflicts of interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and declare real, perceived or potential conflicts promptly; recuse when appropriate; adhere to the Conflict of Interest and Confidentiality Agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications should be treated as strictly confidential at all times by those involved in the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not share deliberations or application content outside meetings; secure access, storage and transmission of documents; return or destroy materials after use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of duties
rubrics_metrics.description: SSHRC separates the merit review of proposals from funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committees assess merit; SSHRC staff/executives make funding decisions based on committee recommendations and budget availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: No parallel assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: SSHRC avoids assessing the merit of the same proposal more than once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure applications are not evaluated multiple times in parallel processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of Interest and Confidentiality policy (tri-agency)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Conflict of Interest and Confidentiality policy applies to CIHR, NSERC and SSHRC (the agencies) and governs reviewer conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before accessing applications sign the required agreement; notify program officer of unclear situations; program officers advise on conflicts; those conflicted must recuse (e.g., leave room); chair conflicts require alternate chairing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing conflicts of interest (responsibilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members are responsible for identifying and declaring any conflict of interest, real, perceived or potential, related to an application, and for informing SSHRC staff as soon as they become aware of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to report conflicts is a breach of the Tri‑Agency Framework; individuals under investigation must temporarily withdraw and decline invitations until cleared by agency president.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to Information Act and Privacy Act (implications)
rubrics_metrics.description: All information provided to SSHRC is subject to the Access to Information Act and the Privacy Act; applicants have statutory rights to access certain assessment materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants can access full text of external assessments and appraisals but not reviewer names or comments about others; Partnership Grants panels are an exception for reviewer names in co-authored reports released after review completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal information handling and security
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members must protect and keep confidential all application information; ensure secure access, storage and transmission; return or securely delete materials after meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safeguard extranet credentials and removable media; contact ATIP-AIPRP@sshrc-crsh.gc.ca for privacy questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on reviewers using public generative AI tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Inputting application information into publicly available generative AI tools could breach privacy and intellectual property; use of such tools for evaluating applications is strictly prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use online tools such as ChatGPT or DeepL to evaluate or process application text; doing so may violate confidentiality agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee deliberations confidentiality and limits on extra-application information
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee discussions are confidential and members must not impart, refer to, or consider information about the applicant that does not appear in the application materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decline applicant inquiries about decisions and refer them to SSHRC; do not disclose results before SSHRC release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics compliance (TCPS‑2)
rubrics_metrics.description: All research funding recipients must comply with the Tri‑Council Policy Statement: Ethical Conduct for Research Involving Humans (TCPS 2), including Chapter 9 for research with Indigenous Peoples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should support adherence; committees may raise ethics concerns but applicants are not required to submit ethics certificates with applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible Conduct of Research (raising concerns)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tri‑Agency Framework describes requirements for applying for and managing funds and outlines processes for allegations of breaches of agency policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee members can raise concerns (e.g., plagiarism, inaccurate CV claims) with chair or program officer before the meeting; such concerns should not be considered when assessing merit; program officer forwards concerns to Secretariat on Responsible Conduct of Research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Under SSHRC’s Non‑Discrimination Policy, eligible persons will not be subject to discrimination under any SSHRC funding activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure assessments do not discriminate; apply eligibility requirements fairly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias awareness and mandatory training
rubrics_metrics.description: The agencies developed tri‑agency Bias in Peer Review training modules to help identify and mitigate bias; modules launched March 2026 and are mandatory after April 1, 2026, for those who haven't completed equivalent training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete required anti-bias training; apply learnings to identify and address bias in deliberations; refer to Canada’s Anti‑Racism Strategy 2024–2028.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility accommodations
rubrics_metrics.description: SSHRC is committed to maximizing accessibility and inclusiveness of review processes and creating inclusive meetings is a shared responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accommodations on request, schedule breaks, encourage timely material submission, chair should summarize conclusions; contact accessibility-accessibilite@sshrc-crsh.gc.ca for assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official languages equity
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are accepted in either English or French and are to be treated equitably; program officers provide service in applicant’s language of choice and committees have balanced representation of both official languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee deliberations can occur in either language; treat applications equitably and support official language minority communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals process
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal process managed through SSHRC’s Vice‑President, Corporate Affairs’ office allows applicants to seek reconsideration of a funding decision under certain circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to SSHRC’s Appeals of decisions based on merit review for details on grounds and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee chair responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The chair ensures the committee carries out work with fairness, thoroughness and integrity, observes policies, manages time and ensures final recommendations reflect consensus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guide discussions, ensure respectful inclusive deliberations, manage time with program officer, officially approve final scores and ranking, address interpersonal conflicts, lead policy discussions and take on additional reviewing as needed; for grant competitions, chairs should be familiar with all applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee member responsibilities and scoring practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members receive assessment tools and assigned applications, must check conflicts, submit preliminary scores, and score using the funding opportunity’s evaluation criteria and scoring table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the full spectrum of the evaluation scale to help establish rank; provide strengths/weaknesses notes if provided; consider budgets for assigned applications; recuse immediately on conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program officer responsibilities in review
rubrics_metrics.description: Program officers act as SSHRC representatives, ensuring eligibility, assigning applications, providing guidance, and ensuring consistent application of policies and evaluation criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support chair in fostering inclusive environment; prepare provisional rank-ordered list from preliminary scores; serve as meeting secretary (record scores, recommendations, concerns); prepare results packages and feedback for applicants; advise on problematic applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: SSHRC observers role
rubrics_metrics.description: Observers may be invited to attend meetings to make recommendations to SSHRC management on policies, procedures and evaluation criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observers do not participate in committee discussions and are subject to conflict of interest and confidentiality agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-meeting review and preliminary scoring process
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members must review assigned applications, check conflicts, submit preliminary scores to program officer and may be asked for written comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program officer compiles preliminary scores and produces initial ranking used to determine discussion order; additional reviewers may be asked if scores vary significantly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of external assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: For some opportunities SSHRC solicits external assessments to assist the committee; committees should distance themselves from external assessments that contain unprofessional, discriminatory or biased comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate in writing if an external assessment is unprofessional when providing feedback to an applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orientation and calibration meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Some committees hold orientation and calibration meetings to ensure consistent use of evaluation criteria and scoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calibration involves scoring sample applications, discussing differences, and adjusting scores to improve consistency across reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussing applications during meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are discussed based on preliminary scores, with the first reviewer summarizing strengths and weaknesses and offering a recommendation; others add comments related to evaluation criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to explain reasoning when assigned scores differ significantly; discuss applications with large score discrepancies in greater detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reaching consensus on scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on discussion, committee members arrive at an overall consensus score for each application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program officer may consult the committee to draft brief feedback for applicants after consensus is reached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ranking applications and finalization
rubrics_metrics.description: At the end of discussions the committee finalizes a rank-ordered list of applications which is approved by the chair; after this step rankings cannot be changed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some opportunities have minimum score or rank cutoffs for funding; the final list is submitted to SSHRC senior management for funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy and procedure feedback from committees
rubrics_metrics.description: Following the meeting, the committee may hold a policy discussion to inform SSHRC staff of difficulties encountered, best practices and program issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members may also provide electronic feedback; SSHRC uses this input to improve processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for the merit review of Indigenous research (operational rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application fits SSHRC’s definition of Indigenous research the reviewer should assess it against the Challenge, Feasibility and Capability criteria by consulting the Guidelines for the merit review of Indigenous research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidelines complement TCPS‑2 Chapter 9 and are relevant for Indigenous and non-Indigenous researchers conducting research with Indigenous Peoples; contact program officer with questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for effective research training (assessment focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines assist in promoting effective research training and career development and are applicable across SSHRC funding opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee members should use the guidelines to gauge quality of proposed training activities and support provided by host institutions; applicants should include relevant training dimensions in proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research-creation eligibility and assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Research-creation is an eligible activity across SSHRC funding opportunities and should be evaluated according to disciplinary standards and creative/artistic merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult Guidelines for research-creation support materials and specific applicant resources for Insight Grant and Insight Development Grant committees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on use of artificial intelligence in applications
rubrics_metrics.description: SSHRC does not discourage the use of AI in application development or research; researchers remain responsible for the content of their applications and must disclose AI use if they choose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Known or suspected AI use should not factor into evaluation; reviewers should focus on whether the project meets program criteria; proposing AI as methodology should be assessed according to disciplinary norms. Reviewers are strictly prohibited from using publicly available generative AI tools for evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of career interruptions and special circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Committees are asked to consider career interruptions and special circumstances that affected researchers’ records as defined in funding opportunity instructions (typically over the last six years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows fairer assessment of research experience and contributions independent of interruptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible Research Assessment (DORA principles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies endorse DORA and encourage assessment of research on its own merit rather than proxies like journal prestige; reviewers should avoid using metrics such as journal impact factor and h-index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value diverse research outputs and impacts (training, knowledge mobilization, policy influence, creative outputs); consider refereed and non-refereed contributions, forthcoming works, creative outputs, and non-academic contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research contributions — acceptable types to consider
rubrics_metrics.description: Research contributions can include refereed outputs (books, articles, conference proceedings), non‑refereed outputs (book reviews, reports, policy papers), forthcoming contributions, creative outputs, and contributions to non‑academic audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate creative outputs by disciplinary standards; include training and knowledge mobilization contributions when assessing excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of Capability subcriteria in CVs (grant applications only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Capability subcriteria should be addressed in the SSHRC CV (and Canadian Common CV or tri‑agency CV as applicable) and may also be addressed in main application sections or Participants involvement sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee members should consult the CV and application sections to assess Capability subcriteria for grant applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge mobilization plan assessment (grant applications only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members are asked to evaluate the knowledge mobilization plan according to the related Feasibility subcriterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SSHRC Guidelines for effective knowledge mobilization and application instructions to assess appropriateness and feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access and research data management expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant holders must comply with the Tri‑Agency Open Access Policy on Publications and the Tri‑Agency Research Data Management Policy; SSHRC recognizes Indigenous data sovereignty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectations: results made openly available when possible; data responsibly and securely managed and reusable where ethically and legally allowable; consider distinctions‑based approaches for Indigenous data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected outcomes summary evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Expected outcomes are potential benefits of the proposed project (e.g., curriculum enhancements, graduate supervision, enriched public discourse, improved policy, business strategies, innovations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee members should evaluate the expected outcomes summary according to any related Challenge subcriteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for support of tools for research and related activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines assist in assessing funding requests for tools distinct from typical grant components; applicants must list tool expenses and justify them in the budget justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee members should assess whether tool purpose/use is directly linked to objectives (Overall), evaluate the tool under the Challenge criterion’s appropriateness of methods/approach, and consider the budget under the Feasibility criterion. Fail the application on Feasibility if tool activities cannot be carried out within budget limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing budget proposals and determining grant size (principles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Committees review budgets to determine whether requested amounts are appropriate; use the principle of minimum essential funding to guide budget discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on overall merit regardless of budget size; each grant must receive a passing score on Challenge, Feasibility and Capability to be recommended. Reflect budget weaknesses in the Feasibility score. Recommend budget reductions/reallocations where savings are possible without jeopardizing objectives. Consider type of institution (e.g., travel needs for isolated institutions). Committees will not adjust budgets for applications not recommended for funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use of grant funds and financial administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must justify all proposed budget expenditures; SSHRC staff may indicate whether expenses are an appropriate use of grant funds and the Tri‑Agency Guide on Financial Administration governs post‑award administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article processing charges for open access journals and book processing charges are appropriate expenses but committees should consider realism of publication plans, target publishers/journals, commensurateness of costs, and options for less expensive outlets or self‑archiving. Consult program officer for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple-source funding (assessment rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants can fund project components from multiple sources and this is not grounds for reducing an applicant’s budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Insight Grant and Insight Development Grant availability of other funding is generally beneficial but not obligatory; applicants must indicate there is no duplication of financial support for budget items.
